chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: Boston's Ken Club and a band with James P. Johnson
summary: He takes bands to the Ken Club in Boston, one with James P. Johnson and Kaiser Marshall, after a Chicago club is shut down for serving sailors.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And, then you went to Boston and did the Ken Club and a few other things in that same period too---
Yes -- Pee Wee and Brad Gowans
And, you had a band and you went and played in Chicago and then you went into Boston.
The greatest band I ever took there was -- I had James P. Johnson and Kaiser Marshall---
Yeah - and Rod Cless and a drummer from Chicago - I just can't remember his name now---

That only one time -- but I had another band with a drummer from Chicago and I had Jack Church again with me there and I did the Ken Club quite a bit you know - back and forth (inaudible); I first met (inaudible) from Chicago there.

And, I had been playing in Chicago in a place that got closed down; I was just there from New York and it got closed down for selling two sailors under--age--- whiskey and that would happen to me - wouldn't it?
So, they closed the place down and I went back---
That was really your first time back in Chicago since you had left about ten years before - right?

Yes, really to play and it got slowed; ; we got the chance to go to the Ken Club so I took the band -- I even had Gene Schroeder in that one and the Chicago drummer; we went to the Ken Club in an old Packard that I had and we got there and did a hell of a job.
